guide.starrail_sim.help.title: Path System Guide
guide.starrail_sim.help.open_current: Press P to open the character attributes screen.
guide.starrail_sim.help.path: Selecting a Path does not place a ruin until you click Confirm Path Search. Travel to the displayed anchor, open its chest, and use the matching Trial Token to start that Path's initial trial. Each player can have only one pending ruin clue at a time. The token is consumed only after the trial starts successfully.
guide.starrail_sim.help.practice: Every practice reward is at most +1; a hit, skill and kill from one attack never pay twice. Paths use separate eligibility and reward intervals. R7:each 300 practice grants +10%% Attack, max 10 times.
guide.starrail_sim.help.trial: The matching ruin Trial Token starts the initial trial; completing both objectives enters the Path automatically. The token is not returned after an initial trial fails or times out; seek again and obtain a new one to retry. Afterward, reaching a practice target automatically starts a rank-up trial, which also ranks up automatically when both objectives are complete.
guide.starrail_sim.help.progress: The ruin anchor stays visible in the lower-left messages and on the Path Search screen. You cannot seek another ruin while a clue is pending. If no site meets the 400-block horizontal spacing, move farther away and retry. The Path Guide explains each trial objective.
guide.starrail_sim.help.rollback: Resetting a path removes its current effects, but keeps its unlocked rank, practice progress, and completed Path Veteran practice milestones.
guide.starrail_sim.path.preservation.cor: Practice Preservation through blocking and enduring damage, focusing on defense and survival.
guide.starrail_sim.path.preservation.goa: Block 3 attacks and survive after taking 5 hostile damage.
guide.starrail_sim.path.preservation.pra: Accumulate 3 actual blocks or 6 actual hostile damage for +1, sharing a 12s reward interval. Both tallies reset on reward.
guide.starrail_sim.path.preservation.tip: From R2, gain a shield every 10 seconds; yellow hearts can stack up to 2.5 times your current Armor. From R4, successfully block hostile mob attacks with your shield to build Guard. Ordinary hits, player attacks, and failed blocks do not count. Guard stacks to 3 and expires if you do not block again for 8 seconds. Barrier has a 6-second cooldown.
guide.starrail_sim.path.preservation.mec:
R2: every 10s gain absorption equal to armor, capped at armor x2.5.
R4: actual blocks build 3 Guard stacks for 8s.
R5: barrier gives Resistance II for 10s, cooldown 6s; cannot retrigger while active.
R6: later barrier blocks counter for armor x20%.
R7: Resistance III for 15s and armor x50% counter.
guide.starrail_sim.path.destruction.core: Fight while endangered or at low health, turning damage taken into destructive power.
guide.starrail_sim.path.destruction.goal: Defeat 3 hostile mobs below 50% health and take 10 damage.
guide.starrail_sim.path.destruction.prac: Kill at <=50% health for +1. Accumulate 8 actual hostile damage at low health for an auxiliary +1, every 15s. A kill clears the damage tally and restarts that interval.
guide.starrail_sim.path.destruction.tips: Destruction rewards fighting while endangered. Defeating enemies or taking damage at low health grants practice; a flawless fight is not the only way to progress. Higher-rank mechanics turn damage taken into Wrath and Burning Soul, but watch your health so you do not fall before the bonuses activate.
guide.starrail_sim.path.destruction.mech:
R4: <=50% health grants +10% direct damage.
R5: low-health hostile damage builds 3 Wrath stacks for 8s.
R6: full Wrath grants next-hit +35%, usable within 8s.
R7: <=25% health starts +50% damage and Resistance I for 8s, cooldown 12s. Healing does not cancel the buff. Direct skill bonuses add up to +95%; derived damage is never multiplied twice.
guide.starrail_sim.path.hunt.core: Focus on defeating enemies and maintaining a hunting streak, emphasizing single-target damage and critical hits.
guide.starrail_sim.path.hunt.goals: Defeat 5 hostile mobs and complete 2 hunting streaks.
guide.starrail_sim.path.hunt.practice: Defeat a hostile for +1 practice. No extra cooldown; one attack with multiple kills pays at most once.
guide.starrail_sim.path.hunt.tips: Kills advance the hunting streak. Hunt Intent stacks up to 3 times, and the rhythm is lost after 8 seconds without another kill. From Rank 5, the next attack while Intent is active gains Pursuit Strike; Rank 6 critical hits can maintain Intent; Rank 7 Reverse Pursuit has its own cooldown.
guide.starrail_sim.path.hunt.mechanics:
R4: kills build up to 3 intent stacks for 8s.
R5: full intent empowers the next landed direct hit x1.25.
R6: critical hits refresh active intent.
R7: Reverse Pursuit x1.50, 8s cooldown; no weaker pursuit during cooldown. Trace cooldown reduction still applies.
guide.starrail_sim.path.erudition.core: Practice Erudition through multi-target hits, chain damage, and area combat.
guide.starrail_sim.path.erudition.goals: Complete 1 multi-target hit, then complete 3 multi-target hits within 30 seconds.
guide.starrail_sim.path.erudition.practi: Hit >=2 distinct hostiles in one direct attack, or complete rank-six analysis, for +1. Both share an 8s interval; secondary damage never counts.
guide.starrail_sim.path.erudition.tips: Erudition requires one attack to hit at least 2 enemies. Area attacks, piercing attacks, and controlled grouping make this easier; repeatedly hitting one enemy does not advance multi-target practice. At higher ranks, multi-target hits build Analysis and trigger Knowledge Echo, while Final Calculation strengthens one area attack.
guide.starrail_sim.path.erudition.mechan:
R4: echo hits 1 other enemy within 2.5 blocks for 15% of direct-hit damage, cooldown 1.2s.
R5:3 blocks,2 enemies,20%.
R6: directly hit 3 distinct enemies within 5s for next-hit x1.20 within 6s.
R7: >=2 other enemies within 3 blocks triggers 45% damage within 4 blocks, cooldown 12s. Secondary hits cannot retrigger skills or analysis.
guide.starrail_sim.path.harmony.core: Use food and resonance states to support combat, emphasizing buffs and cooperation.
guide.starrail_sim.path.harmony.goals: Eat 3 food items to trigger resonance and defeat 3 enemies while resonating.
guide.starrail_sim.path.harmony.practice: A kill during path resonance grants +1. Three combat food uses can grant auxiliary +1 every 30s; eligible food uses are >=10s apart and require combat within 10s. Kills clear auxiliary progress.
guide.starrail_sim.path.harmony.tips: Food builds Resonance, and continuing to fight while resonating completes the trial. Harmony focuses on sustained support: Rank 5 Afterglow strengthens the next 3 attacks during Resonance, Rank 6 Concert Echo restores health after a kill during Resonance, and Rank 7 Unified Resonance grants Absorption and extends Resonance on kills.
guide.starrail_sim.path.harmony.mechanic:
Food grants path resonance for 15s, R4:20s. Other Resistance sources are not resonance.
R5: next 3 attacks +5%.
R6: resonance kill heals 2.5% max health, cooldown 5s.
R7: food ensures 2.5% absorption for 5s; kills extend resonance by 3s, up to 30s remaining. Repeated food refreshes, not stacks; expiry removes only remaining owned shield.
guide.starrail_sim.path.nihility.core: Apply Nihility Erosion, weaken enemies, and deal damage over time through negative effects.
guide.starrail_sim.path.nihility.goals: Apply Nihility Erosion 5 times and defeat 3 eroded enemies.
guide.starrail_sim.path.nihility.practic: New main-target erosion grants +1 at most every 10s. Killing your eroded enemy pays +1 only if it has never paid before. Each enemy grants at most one point in its lifetime.
guide.starrail_sim.path.nihility.tips: Nihility first applies negative effects, then uses damage over time and echoes to gain an advantage. Higher Effect Hit Rate makes Erosion less likely to be blocked by enemy Effect Resistance. Erosion deals periodic damage, while higher-rank mechanics can spread it or trigger a burst when it ends.
guide.starrail_sim.path.nihility.mechani:
Erosion: Weakness I and 1 magic damage each second for 5s; R4:7s, with all scheduled pulses.
R5: new erosion spreads within 2.5 blocks to 1 unmarked enemy, without recursive spread.
R6: periodic damage 1.5.
R7: your eroded enemy death applies erosion and 2 magic damage within 3 blocks; no cooldown, no recursive same-burst chain.
guide.starrail_sim.path.abundance.core: Practice Abundance through healing and repeated recovery, focusing on sustain and max health.
guide.starrail_sim.path.abundance.goals: Restore 10 health in total and complete 3 separate healing events.
guide.starrail_sim.path.abundance.practi: Restore 6 health actually lost to hostiles for +1 every 12s. Injury credit expires after 30s; environmental self-harm, overhealing and shields do not count. Same-tick healing is merged.
guide.starrail_sim.path.abundance.tips: Healing yourself or allies advances Abundance practice, and separate healing events count separately. Excess healing can become damage absorption; Rank 6 Renewal heals based on max health, while Rank 7 Mercy provides stronger emergency protection with a long cooldown.
guide.starrail_sim.path.abundance.mechan:
R4: healing below 80% health grants Regeneration I for 3s, cooldown 5s; regeneration cannot perpetually refresh itself.
R5: convert 50% overhealing to absorption, max 4 per event; owned overflow shield capped at 20% max health.
R6: healing below 50% grants Resistance I for 2s, cooldown 8s.
R7: prevent lethal damage, set health to 1, heal 20% max health (healing bonuses apply) and ensure 5% absorption, cooldown 60s.
guide.starrail_sim.path.remembrance.core: Record combat memories and trigger echoes, emphasizing repeated hits and memory buildup.
guide.starrail_sim.path.remembrance.goal: Record 3 memories and hit the same enemy again within 8 seconds to trigger 2 echoes.
guide.starrail_sim.path.remembrance.prac: A valid echo grants +1 every 8s. Recording, refreshing and Eternal Echo do not add duplicate rewards.
guide.starrail_sim.path.remembrance.tips: Remembrance rewards repeatedly connecting with the same target: after recording a memory, hit that target again within the memory window to trigger an echo. The base window is 8 seconds and becomes 12 seconds at Rank 4; keep one target selected instead of switching constantly.
guide.starrail_sim.path.remembrance.mech:
Record, then echo on same target within 8s for +1 damage; R4:12s and +2.
R5: same-target follow-up x1.10 within 5s.
R6: retain memory, echo interval 3s.
R7: every 3 echoes x1.50, cooldown 10s; at most 3 stored echoes while cooling down.
guide.starrail_sim.path.elation.core: Build momentum through consecutive hits and Elation bursts, emphasizing combos and unexpected bursts.
guide.starrail_sim.path.elation.goals: Complete 8 consecutive hits and trigger 2 Elation bursts; do not wait more than 5 seconds between hits.
guide.starrail_sim.path.elation.practice: A three-hit burst grants +1 every 8s. Ordinary hits and the grand burst do not pay extra.
guide.starrail_sim.path.elation.tips: Elation builds momentum through consecutive hits and triggers bursts when the rhythm reaches its conditions. Keep attacks close together, then use the burst to amplify damage. Higher ranks improve the combo window and the number or strength of burst triggers.
guide.starrail_sim.path.elation.mechanic:
Combo window 5s, R5:7s. Every third hit adds 2 damage, R5:4.
R4: equal chance for Strength I 5s, Regeneration I 3s, Luck I 10s or Resistance I 2s.
R6: next 2 hits x1.10, refreshed rather than stacked.
R7: every sixth hit x1.50, cooldown 10s and 2 distinct extra random buffs; ordinary bursts still trigger during cooldown.
guide.starrail_sim.help.damage: Damage numbers: normal damage is a white negative number; critical damage is a white negative number with an exclamation mark; damage over time also uses white numbers. Toughness damage is red, and a break hit is red with an exclamation mark.
guide.starrail_sim.help.toughness: Toughness: normal enemies have 10 base Toughness, elite enemies have 20, and bosses have 30. Each direct attack deals health damage and removes 1 Toughness at the same time, so health and Toughness are reduced together.
guide.starrail_sim.help.break: Break: when an enemy reaches zero Toughness, it enters the Broken state for 10 seconds. Toughness recovers from 0% to 100% over 20 seconds. Break hits deal additional break damage, and Break Effect improves the break payoff.
guide.starrail_sim.help.effect_hit: Effect Hit Rate: determines whether a negative effect can be applied. Nihility Erosion, damage over time, and higher-rank echoes make an Effect Hit check first; more Effect Hit Rate is more reliable against resistant enemies.
guide.starrail_sim.help.effect_resistanc: Effect Resistance: a target's ability to resist negative effects. It affects application, not an effect that has already succeeded; when the notification says an effect was resisted, that attempt did not apply.
guide.starrail_sim.help.knockback_resist: Knockback Resistance: reduces the distance or chance of being knocked back by attacks. It is separate from Armor, Armor Toughness, and Effect Resistance, and mainly affects positioning and combat rhythm.
guide.starrail_sim.help.relic_access: Press P to open Character Details and choose Relics. The page operates on real relics in your inventory and Curios slots. Equipping, unequipping, enhancing and salvaging update player items; this is not a separate preview copy.
guide.starrail_sim.help.relic_slots: The outer ring has Head, Hands, Body and Feet slots. The inner ring has Planar Sphere and Link Rope slots. Relic details and tooltips show the set, rarity, main stat and substats.
guide.starrail_sim.help.relic_trial: Choose an outer- or inner-ring set at the arena's central device. Defeat 3 waves of 4 enemies to receive 1–3 random relics from that set. Reward count, rarity, and stats are locked when the battle starts; rarity follows the owner's Path rank: rank 1 can drop 2–3 stars, ranks 2–4 improve gradually, and rank 5 or higher guarantees 5 stars. Ordinary floating ruins and Relic Duel Arenas naturally generate across The Path's Clear Sky Meadow and Firefly Grove. Arena generation does not require flat terrain: it clears the footprint and builds foundations beneath low areas. Only vanilla hostile mobs are selected; creepers, vexes, phantoms, and vanilla bosses are excluded. Mobs added by other mods are never summoned. Operators can locate one with /starrail arena locate [dimension]; use /starrail arena pool [all|normal|ranged] to list candidates or /starrail arena inspect namespace:entity_id to see why an entity was included or excluded. The arena_allowed, arena_excluded, and arena_ranged tags can adjust risk filtering, exclusions, and ranged classification for vanilla hostile mobs only; they cannot add modded mobs. To build the 25×25 test arena manually, stand at a clear site and run /starrail arena build [dimension].
guide.starrail_sim.help.relic_growth: A substat is added or enhanced every 3 enhancement levels. Maximum levels are +6 for 2-star, +9 for 3-star, +12 for 4-star and +15 for 5-star relics. Enhancement consumes Lost Crystals; the page previews the level and stat changes.
guide.starrail_sim.help.relic_salvage: Salvaging relics yields enhancement materials; a 5-star relic can instead yield Relic Remains. Equipped, locked or pending-reroll relics cannot be salvaged. Relic Remains craft 5-star relics; targeted main stats require Self-Modeling Resin, while targeting four substat types requires an Interference Key (crafted for 500 Relic Remains). Targeted relics start with those four types at +0; roll tiers and enhancement rolls remain random.
guide.starrail_sim.help.relic_reroll: Variable Dice reroll how substat enhancement rolls are distributed on a fully enhanced 5-star relic. They do not change substat types or their initial values. Review the new candidate before choosing the old or new result. Equipped or locked relics cannot be rerolled.
guide.starrail_sim.help.relic_sets: Set effects use the number of matching relics actually equipped in Curios. The 2-piece and 4-piece effects activate when their thresholds are met. The Relics page and item tooltips show set effects and current piece counts.
guide.starrail_sim.help.attributes: Attribute details: click any attribute panel to inspect its base value, bonuses from paths or other sources, and final value. Percentage attributes are calculated from the corresponding base attribute.
guide.starrail_sim.help.practice_detail: Practice: each path counts actions that match its own theme. The Paths screen shows current practice and its target; the Nine Paths page explains the specific way to practice each path.
guide.starrail_sim.help.path_switch: Path switching: after the initial trial, you automatically enter the selected path. You can have only one current path; resetting it removes current path effects but keeps unlocked ranks and practice.
guide.starrail_sim.help.notifications: Path skill notices use their path color and appear above the player HUD; trial progress updates in real time. View practice totals in the Paths screen instead of expecting a notice for each point.
guide.starrail_sim.help.future: Light Cones, all nine Path Trace trees and the Relics system are available through Character Details. Matching Trace materials can be obtained from Path ruin guardians and repeat challenges.
guide.starrail_sim.help.light_cone: Light Cones are available. Open Light Cone from Character Details to inspect base stats, superimposition and Path-exclusive effects; exclusive effects activate only on the matching Path. Traces are also available: open Traces to inspect your current Path tree and spend matching materials to unlock nodes. Rolling back nodes or resetting Traces refunds spent materials. No Trace tree appears while unaligned.

tooltip.starrail_sim.where_dreams_belong: At the edge of the Asdana system, the Memory Zone surged like a stormy sea. She was a spark, ready to go out in the gale.

Insects blotted out the sky as they broke through the front line. Wrapped in flame, she flew toward them; their ashes fell like snow over the black remains of the knights.

tooltip.starrail_sim.memory_of_me.story_: When the plum blossoms were about to fade, she liked to preserve that moment and keep it by her side.
Many years passed. Noisy, sweet, and all kinds of life were born from her hands, yet the plum blossoms still fell on schedule.
Many years passed. Her reflection never changed, but on the scale of the cosmos, could she too remain vivid for only a fleeting instant?
‘If all things must pass away, what meaning is there in creation?’
No one knew how long the silence lasted. The wind stirred the falling blossoms, and the reflection answered as it always had.

tooltip.starrail_sim.make_farewell_more_: Another farewell ceremony.
Treading upon shattered moonlight, the girl weaves a wreath of farewell by the riverside.
An ancient elegy freezes in the cold air; the quiet river flows toward a distant land of flowers.
A bloodstained book, a rusted sword, a handkerchief embroidered with verse... She accepts their keepsakes, and the stories of their lives.
“My eyes are like a lens, forever longing for the stars.”
An epitaph for a scholar who died too young.
“To life and death, a knight gives only a cold glance.”
The life's creed of an unnamed warrior.
“Life is but death, shining for a fleeting moment.”
The final line written with the life of a poet who sought eternity.

Veils, garlands, long skirts—the wind carries blessings.

tooltip.starrail_sim.trace_material.abun: A beautiful flower grown from the Seed of Life. Greatly boosts Traces for those on the Path of Abundance.
The power of Abundance gathers in its pistils, and it will never wither.
Neither flame, frost, nor any other adversity can slow its growth.
In time, its leaves will feed on starlight, while its roots take the flesh of all beings as soil,
joining into one, undying and eternal. Its fruit will promise immortality.
“There are colossal vessels, greater than mountains, gliding through the void. Upon them grows an undying tree, whose fruit grants longevity.”
tooltip.starrail_sim.trace_material.harm: An intricately made music box of unknown origin. Greatly boosts Traces for those on the Path of Harmony.
It plays a cosmic symphony that shakes the soul.
“Some astronomers believe that celestial bodies move like parts of a complex machine, and that the sun, moon, and stars sound crystal-clear notes as they turn.
This is what they call the ‘music of the spheres.’”
tooltip.starrail_sim.trace_material.nihi: A solid mass of dark matter captured from the void. Greatly boosts Traces for those on the Path of Nihility.
The faint-hearted need only glance at its facets to sink into chaos for all eternity.
tooltip.starrail_sim.trace_material.pres: A curious great shield, adorned with amber quarried beyond the stars. Greatly boosts Traces for those on the Path of Preservation.
Its bearer seems protected by an unseen wall. Neither flame-filled arrows
nor claws as vast as mountains can harm them.
Legend tells of an ancient war: tribal heroes bearing bronze shields
stood beside warriors with blazing spears, charging the ancient beasts in a desperate assault.
This shield bears witness to that battle.
tooltip.starrail_sim.trace_material.erud: A phantom key seen in the hands of the galaxy’s greatest geniuses. Greatly boosts Traces for those on the Path of Erudition.
Proof of invitation, capable of opening the doors to the halls of Erudition.
The key is in your hand, yet finding the door it opens is harder than obtaining the key itself.
Those who pass through will realize there is no turning back once they enter.
“Erudition cannot tell you the answer to the universe, but it can teach you how to ask.”
tooltip.starrail_sim.trace_material.dest: A damaged weapon left behind by a member of the Antimatter Legion. Greatly boosts Traces for those on the Path of Destruction.
This weapon represents its owner's rank in the Legion and their deeds in the name of Destruction.
Its owner was tasked with appearing at the war's end, kindling a blaze to burn the world.
No matter which Aeon blessed it, no matter how glorious its former legacy,
this planet will become dying embers, fading in the depths of space.
“Bearer of this seal, you are tasked with cleansing the world.”
tooltip.starrail_sim.trace_material.hunt: A fragment of the sky-piercing arrow shot by the Reignbow. Greatly boosts Traces for those on the Path of the Hunt.
A remnant of a divine miracle no mortal could witness. It crossed light-years and shattered a star,
and people can only imagine its power from the arrow's dying embers.
Only the Xianzhou's artisan leader, the Master Artificer, may reforge these fragments
and present them to a hero of peerless achievement.
“Stars split, skies fall; its light shines through the ages.”
tooltip.starrail_sim.trace_material.reme: Another form of life: matter the universe cannot forget. Greatly boosts Traces for those on the Path of Remembrance.
It ripened into a net that gathers history, a flower grown from the past.
Life is its garden, and may also become its heart.
If you become that heart, you will remember the universe, and the universe will remember you—
“Memory is the substance of all things; thus, in the pure land without defilement, nothing is born or lost.”
tooltip.starrail_sim.trace_material.elat: A paperback edition of “The Celestial Journey of the Fluffy.” Greatly boosts Traces for those on the Path of Elation.
Its obi strip bears many endorsements, including those from Zhenzhu, Jade, Aventurine, Topaz,
Dr. Ratio, Jing Yuan, Feixiao, Huaiyan, Yao Guang, Hua, Kafka, Robin, Zaitian, Schneider,
Duke Inferno, Hoolay, Rongi, Sparkle, Sparkle, and the Trailblazer—all famous across the cosmos.
Later, Teacher Mofu paid dearly for “fabricated endorsements and false advertising.”
“Attorney Umbrella, these petty-minded celebrities are teaming up to sue me. I want to hire you to defend me, will you?”
“Hahaha, you must be joking. I still have a life to live.”

guide.starrail_sim.path.material_source: Defeating this path ruin guardian has a 30% chance to drop 1 matching Trace material. The first-clear chest supplies a dedicated reusable seal; use the anchor beside the chest to challenge the guardian again. Each rematch kill starts a 30-second cooldown. guide.starrail_sim.help.hud_values: Status bars: by default, the HUD sits above experience, with each number following its icon. The green main bar shows current/max health and the gold main bar shows hunger; blue and pale-green secondary bars show absorption and saturation. Absorption is a separate shield, not maximum health. Its bar is relative to maximum health; the actual amount remains visible even when the bar is full. Armor and toughness show actual attribute values. Low health, low hunger, damage and recovery have local visual feedback.
guide.starrail_sim.help.hud_context: Context: bubbles and remaining breathing seconds appear underwater or while air is not full. Living mounts show current/max health, and jumpable mounts also show a short charge meter. These readings share the lower row with absorption. A central gap leaves room for experience levels; if a long level number overlaps, status icons and readings take priority. This survival HUD is hidden in Creative and Spectator modes; F1 hides the HUD.
guide.starrail_sim.help.hud_settings: Display settings: F8 toggles between the mod HUD and vanilla by default; rebind it in Controls. The Display Settings button at the top right of this guide changes smooth drawing, motion, HUD style and placement, 75%-100% scale, and number format. UI text uses Minecraft's active default font. Choices save immediately and only affect presentation, not attributes or combat.

The sea washed over her ankles, and foam broke beneath the moon. During a rare break in filming, the young woman was invited to a little beachside bonfire.
The firelight stretched the children's shadows. Confusion filled their little faces. They looked at her and asked timidly, “Sister Robin, what should we do?”
She smiled and touched the strings with her fingertips, answering without words.
“Come, follow me—” The first pluck was swallowed by the sea breeze; the second found its tune. With waves on the shore and lights flickering, she sang softly, pouring out the clear sky in her heart.
“When you don't know how to sing, listen to the melody in your heart.”
At first, the notes were scattered. Then they took shape, and the shape began to breathe. She sang, they sang, until the summer breeze passed by.
“Listen, this is the song in our hearts. It has always been there, waiting to be heard.” She heard it, and offered her gentle wish:
“Rise and sing, then spread your wings and fly.”

guide.starrail_sim.help.dimension_entry: Entry and return: The Astral Express is fixed at (0, 280, 0) in the Overworld and (0, 350, 0) in The Path. Activate the Star Rail Beacon inside either train to travel between them. The Path arrival is at (0, 350, 0), and the return point is inside the Overworld train.
guide.starrail_sim.help.dimension_region: Regions: Clear Sky Meadow has open grassland, gentle slopes, river valleys and sparse groves. Firefly Grove has bright woodland, lakeshores and clearings. Starlit Tide Ocean ranges from shallow reefs to deep water and trenches, with seabed ores and sparse bubble vents. Clear Sand Beach connects the land to shallow water along the coast. Riverbed Gravel stays near waterways and low ground, while Clearwater River Sand covers most of the beach. Tide Grass grows on sand or gravel; Clear Sand Bellflower roots only in Clearwater River Sand in Clear Sand Beach. Turtles spawn naturally on these beaches. Starvein Cavern is an underground biome with original Starvein Geodes, rare large crystal chambers, and shared minerals in its walls and rock layers. Starfall Highlands have open rocky slopes, scattered scree, and low cushiongrass. Stilltide Marsh is a lowland of humus soil and scattered shallow pools edged with reeds.
guide.starrail_sim.help.dimension_ruins: Ruins and challenges: Ordinary floating ruins and relic dueling arenas generate naturally in The Path. Start path seeking from the Path screen while inside the dimension; it records a target location. Relic arenas use three waves and the selected set, then award 1–3 random relics on victory.
guide.starrail_sim.help.dimension_naviga: Navigation: The Star Rail Beacon inside each train connects the two fixed hubs. Right-click other beacons to save their coordinates in the Travel Archive and give them a custom name; breaking a recorded beacon removes its coordinates. Operators can use /starrail dimension locate relay to locate the Path train at (0, 350, 0); locate region accepts sunmeadow, glimmerwood, star_tide_ocean, clear_sand_beach, starvein_cavern, star_scree_highlands, or stilltide_marsh. Use ordinary_ruin, relic_trial_arena, or path_ruin for ruins and challenges. locate ore accepts starcoal, dawncopper, suniron, dawn_gold, resonance, memory, starmarrow, stellarjade, or ancientdream; mineral searches only inspect nearby generated chunks and do not generate new ones.
guide.starrail_sim.help.dimension_materi: Shared ores: All seven biomes generate all nine local minerals. Starcoal, Dawn Copper, Suniron and Memory Crystal mainly occur in shallow to middle Path Stone; Dawn Gold, Resonance Crystal, Starmarrow, Stellarjade and Ancient Dream mainly occur in Deep Path Stone. Y ranges: Starcoal 0–96, Dawn Copper -16–112, Suniron -48–96, Memory Crystal -32–48, Dawn Gold -48–24, Resonance Crystal -56–16, Starmarrow -48–16, Stellarjade -56–8, Ancient Dream -60–-32. Higher-tier ores are deeper. Ancient Dream is somewhat less common than Stellarjade, but not dramatically so. Rare Dawn Copper outcrops only try to generate on naturally exposed Path Stone. Operators can use /starrail dimension locate ore <mineral> to search nearby generated chunks; it does not generate new chunks.
guide.starrail_sim.help.dimension_surviv: Survival and progression: Sunmeadow and Firefly trees can be regrown from saplings; their logs make planks and sticks or renewable charcoal. Starcoal works directly as fuel: one burns for 1,600 ticks, and a block crafted from nine burns for 16,000 ticks. Morning Berry Bushes regrow after harvest and can be propagated with berries; Forestbeans grow on farmland and yield pods that can be cooked. Star Tide Algae grows on the seabed, can be replanted, and can be cooked as food. Tide Grass decorates the shore; Clear Sand Bellflower can be replanted, composted, or crafted into light blue dye. Underwater bubble vents form upward currents that serve as vertical landmarks and help you rise to the surface. The Path uses vanilla water, farmland and crop rules. Clear Sky Grass, Clear Sky Dirt, ordinary dirt and humus can be hoed into farmland or shoveled into dirt paths; coarse slope soil first becomes dirt when hoed. Starfall Scree can be collected and placed for terrain detailing. Stilltide Humus can be hoed into farmland or shoveled into a dirt path. Stilltide Reed grows on suitable soil beside water; Starfall Cushiongrass grows on Path grass, coarse slope soil, or Starfall Scree. Both plants can be collected and replanted, but do not grow or spread by themselves. Gear progresses from Suniron to Starmarrow, then smithing templates upgrade it to Netherite-tier Stellarjade and the higher Ancient Dream tier.
